title: Looking for better 3d Animation tools
author: SBelwas
selftext:
I am currently using a combination of Opus 5.5, blender and Meshy to make animations for the game im working on. Results have honestly been pretty bad, at least not to the standard im looking for. 

For context: I've been a software engineer for ~10 years but I am terrible at art. Coding has always been fine for me but the art... not so much. I've not worked on games in the past in part because the art part was always so hard and intimidating. I'd really like to see if anyone has some ai tools that can help me create the things i have in my mind.

comments.body: Interesting! I am using Opus 5.5 with Blender MCP and my model come out amazing after few iteration. replies.body: could you share your results? I also did some blender mcp combination, but honestly maybe the art style, or the limited polygon count or something, but it was quite simplistic. Not bad, works for the job, but could be better imo.

comments.author: Used-Snow-9934
comments.body:
If you want to make it great. Do some fundamental animation training to get an understanding what animation is, bouncing ball, some followthrough exercises, weight shift. Who knows you might even enjoy it more then you know. And that skill will help you with the procedural or generated animations later.  
You could use something like cascadeur to simplify things as well. Seems like a good way to direct animations with the help of ML and physics.

Not interested?  Look what motion capture can do for you, there are even markerless solutions now.  You just need a camera. I think UE has that built in now (at least for metahuman and faces,  you can transfer the animation later to your custom skeleton if you don’t want to use metahuman)

Generative AI can do a lot, it’s amazing, but chose the right tool for the right job.

replies.author: SBelwas
replies.body:
You are 2nd person to recommend cascaduer I will def check that out. 

I guess if I can generate and rig the bas models the actual manipulation of said models feels less scary / hard to learn. I've just failed at every artistic (visual) pursuit I've every tried and I don't wanna adopt false hope.

replies.author: Used-Snow-9934
replies.body:
Yeah, maybe Cascaduer isn't the way to go then. If I were you I'd aim for very simple art.

For example, if I were making a strategy game, I'd use "static models" like pawns. Then I'd just add some squash and stretch to make them feel juicier and bring them to life through animation. Maybe have them jump between tiles, and make sure that jump feels awesome! (And even that isn't easy to get right! So imagine creating an entire character and all its animations.)

You could also make them squash and stretch in response to audio frequencies (if you wanna get technical).

I don't even think you'd need to rig them. You could probably get away with just multiplying the points by a matrix that squashes and stretches the model, if you wanna stick to code.

But if you wanna make something fancier in the long run, rigging a model with a joint and a controller, then animating a jump, would be a good starting point!

comments.author: Brilliant_Ad2977

comments.author: Psychological-Arm42
comments.body:
Directly saying “make it like this blah blah blah” didn’t work for me either. Instead you need to have a lot of stuff setup first.

Have a game design bible (GDD) and buildlog stored in your game folder always (and keep updating them, I use the graphify skill for this to save tokens) and ask the model to load the required parts into context upon each new chat. This way it always knows what the game is, and the design of the game, etc.

once you fix your game art direction, Theme , design and give it enough reference, It more or less knows what’s going to fit in the game. Since claude is notoriously bad at image gen. I use codex for it.

Ask claude to generate a big prompt, to paste into codex, for your required animations / VFX. Ask claude to direct codex to generate an offline chooser website, which generates sprite sheets of all the required animations at 24 fps. Ask it to make 2 or 3 choies for each animation. you can then see the animations at 24 fps and choose the ones u like, give the chosen files to claude, and claude can then add them to the game with good accuracy. It still requires some tweaking and refinement after claude makes it, but its what’s getting the job done for me

comments.author: coding_crow
comments.body: Look at cascadeur for animation. Claude is good at rigging. the missing piece is good base meshes that you won't yet get out of meshy. My workaround is to use existing human bases that are well rigged and weighted. You can generate the clothing, hairstyles, retexture the faces, do pretty much anything with ai, just need a good clean base to start with. (Like the Vroid characters, UMA, MakeHuman or any other solution)

replies.author: SBelwas
replies.body: Thankyou for the recommendation. Really appreciate it

comments.author: Bingeljell
comments.body:
Depending on what you are animating - Kimodo does decent animations. 

I'm working on an end to end text > rigged and animated character pipeline (it's been featured on r/TopologyAI and r/stablediffusion)- and it can spit out some chars with basic animations like idle, walk, run, cheer, jump, etc... 

They're not the best - and that's a thread I plan to fix soon. But in the meantime I just take the output from my pipeline and then just have Opus 5.5 or Sol 6.1 medium take a crack at fixing the animation. It does reasonably well. Since the baseline exists, it can improve it.
